const CACHE_TTL_MS = 5000;

function getCached<T>(key: string): T | null {
  const entry = apiCache.get(key);
  if (entry && Date.now() - entry.timestamp < CACHE_TTL_MS) return entry.data as T;
  return null;
}

function setCache<T>(key: string, data: T) {
  apiCache.set(key, { data, timestamp: Date.now() });
}

/** Flush the API response cache. Exposed for test teardown. */
export function clearApiCache(): void {
  apiCache.clear();
}

codex
The patch introduces multiple blocking packaging and automation problems: the build cannot succeed in clean environments, the documented MCP server command is not runnable, and CI/release are pointed at a non-existent branch. The generated CI templates and MCP server also contain runtime bugs that would surface immediately for common user flows.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Install `src/ui-app` dependencies before invoking `build:ui` — /Users/bobbarclay/GTMCLIAUTOMATION/package.json:55-56
  On a clean checkout, `npm ci` at the repo root does not install `src/ui-app`'s Vite/React dependencies because that package has its own `package.json`/lockfile and the repo is not configured as a workspace. As a result `npm run build` (and the CI/release workflows that call it after only a root `npm ci`) will fail when `cd src/ui-app && npm run build` cannot resolve its local toolchain.

- [P1] Publish a runnable entry point for the MCP server — /Users/bobbarclay/GTMCLIAUTOMATION/package.json:7-9
  The package only exposes the `tagops` binary here, and `src/cli.ts` never registers a `server` subcommand. In a normal install, `npx tagops server` therefore runs `dist/cli.js` and exits with an unknown-command error, so the MCP server described in the README is not actually launchable from the published package.

- [P1] Target the repository's actual default branch in automation — /Users/bobbarclay/GTMCLIAUTOMATION/.github/workflows/ci.yml:3-7
  This repository's actual default branch is `master`, but the new automation is wired to `main` here, and the same mismatch also appears in `release.yml` and `.changeset/config.json`. In the current repo state, pushes and PRs against `master` will never trigger CI or the release pipeline.

- [P1] Remove lint directives from the generated workflow YAML — /Users/bobbarclay/GTMCLIAUTOMATION/src/tools/init-ci.ts:51-52
  These `// eslint-disable-line ...` suffixes are emitted verbatim into the YAML generated by `init-ci`, because they are inside the template literal rather than being TypeScript comments. That makes `GTM_CREDENTIALS`/`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` invalid in every generated workflow, and the same leakage also appends junk arguments to the generated `tagops publish` command later in this file.

- [P2] Report empty GTM workspaces as empty, not as auth failures — /Users/bobbarclay/GTMCLIAUTOMATION/src/server.ts:137-139
  A newly created GTM container can legitimately contain zero tags. This check turns that valid state into `ERROR: Could not list tags. Check GTM auth.`, so MCP clients cannot distinguish an empty workspace from an authentication failure; the same pattern is repeated for triggers and variables below.

- [P2] Handle the no-drift case in the generated drift workflow — /Users/bobbarclay/GTMCLIAUTOMATION/src/tools/init-ci.ts:133-135
  GitHub Actions runs bash steps with `-e -o pipefail`, and `grep -c` exits with status 1 when there are zero matches. In the normal no-drift case, this assignment aborts the generated workflow before the `if [ "$CHANGES" -gt 0 ]` branch runs, so users get a failed drift job instead of the intended `No drift detected.` path.
